items.title: Mississauga driver charged in July Highway 401 double-fatal crash: OPP
items.summary: A 56-year-old Mississauga man is facing criminal charges in connection with a July crash on Highway 401 that left a Cambridge father and daughter dead. m. Investigators say four family members were inside the struck vehicle. An 80-year-old man and his 53-year-old daughter were pronounced dead at the scene. Two other family members were taken to hospital, one with serious injuries and the other with non-life-threatening injuries. The sole occupant of the second vehicle was also taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. The driver has been charged with two counts of dangerous operation causing death and one count of dangerous operation causing bodily harm. The accused was held for a bail hearing last month and was released from custody. A court appearance is scheduled in January, at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton.

items.title: Peel Police Impound Multiple Vehicles After Halloween Weekend Blitz at Mississauga and Brampton Plazas
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say its Safer Roads Team targeted vehicle gatherings at Trinity Common Plaza in Brampton and Derry Financial Plaza in Mississauga over the Halloween weekend. According to police, officers impounded several vehicles for two weeks and handed drivers 30-day licence suspensions as part of the enforcement. The force said photos from the operation show Halloween-themed vehicles, including one covered in fake blood and another wrapped in caution tape, loaded onto flatbed trailers. Police said the crackdown follows years of complaints from residents about loud car rallies and street racing at plazas across Peel, including nearly 20,000 traffic charges laid across Mississauga and Brampton in the first half of 2024. Mississauga's Ridgeway Plaza and Brampton's Trinity Common Mall have both repeatedly drawn these gatherings, prompting Brampton to pass bylaws with fines of $800 to $2,000 for the nuisance. Police said the Safer Roads Team plans to keep up enforcement at both locations.

items.title: Mississauga Library Hosts Its Annual Comic and Gaming Expo This Weekend at the Central Library
items.summary: The Mississauga Library says its annual Comic Expo, known as MCX, returns Nov. 6 and 7 at the Hazel McCallion Central Library on Burnhamthorpe Road. According to organizers, the free, all-ages event is one of the library's most popular annual draws and celebrates comics, games, manga and fandom. The library said visitors can take part in a cosplay red carpet, pose at a green-screen photo booth and browse a trading post for collectibles. Organizers added that the schedule includes workshops and panels on topics like gag comics and miniature building, along with free-play video games and trivia contests. The event comes just days after Halloween, giving costume fans another reason to keep their outfits ready. Admission remains free throughout the weekend, the library said.

items.title: Dangerous driving charges laid in Mississauga crash that killed father, daughter
items.summary: A Mississauga man faces two charges of dangerous driving causing death in a devastating Highway 401 crash this past summer that killed a father and daughter as they were leaving town on vacation. m. in the eastbound express lanes of the busy highway near Dixie Road in Mississauga. Ralph Crane, 80, and his daughter, Sheri-Lynn Crane-Gormley, 53, both of Cambridge, died when the Honda CR-V in which they were passengers was struck from behind by a Mercedes SUV as traffic slowed down during rush-hour conditions. OPP have not released their names, but the two people killed, who were pronounced dead at the scene, were identified earlier in an obituary published by Corbett Funeral Home. Police did say at the time, though, that four people were inside the vehicle when it was rear-ended. “The two other family member occupants were transported to hospital, one with serious injuries and the other with non-life-threatening injuries,” OPP said in a news release on Monday. The driver of the other vehicle, who was the lone occupant, was transported to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police added. L.

items.title: Ontario Provincial Police Lay Charges Months After Fatal Rear-End Crash on Highway 401 in Mississauga
items.summary: Ontario Provincial Police say a Mississauga man faces two charges of dangerous driving causing death after a fatal crash on Highway 401 this past summer. According to OPP, the collision happened in the eastbound express lanes near Dixie Road when a Mercedes SUV rear-ended a Honda CR-V during slow, rush-hour traffic. Police said two of the four people in the CR-V, Ralph Crane, 80, and his daughter Sheri-Lynn Crane-Gormley, 53, both of Cambridge, were pronounced dead at the scene. The other two occupants were taken to hospital, one with serious injuries and the other with non-life-threatening injuries, OPP said. The driver of the Mercedes, its only occupant, was also treated in hospital for non-life-threatening injuries. OPP said the investigation remains ongoing.

items.title: Design Work Wraps Up on Fourth Pumping Station Meant to Curb Flooding in Northwest Mississauga
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says design work is now complete on a fourth automated pumping station meant to reduce chronic flooding in the city's northwest corner. According to Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden, staff expect to award the construction contract for the new station near Osprey Marsh, just south of Osprey Boulevard, once the new term of city council convenes in late November. The city said the project follows a third pumping station that has been running since August along Sixteen Mile Creek, near Doug Leavens Boulevard, in the Lisgar area of west Meadowvale. McFadden said all four stations are designed to regulate stormwater in the Foundation Drain Collector system and automatically pump water out of the sewers once it reaches a set level. City officials have called the new infrastructure critical to protecting homes in the area from major flooding. The fourth station is expected to serve the Osprey Marsh community once it's built.

items.title: Road closures around Ridgeway Plaza in Mississauga
items.summary: A busy intersection in Mississauga’s west end is closed to traffic this week as crews continue to work on widening a main road. The City of Mississauga said it’s closing the Ninth Line/Platinum Drive intersection, to the immediate west of the large Ridgeway Plaza, between Nov. 2 and Nov. 7. The closure is necessary “to facilitate construction of the storm sewer system and oil-grit separator structure” and to allow workers “to safely complete the work while ensuring public safety and the safety of construction personnel,” the city said in its latest project update. Drivers can use Eglinton Avenue and Ridgeway Drive as alternate routes, project officials said, adding detour signs will be posted. The city noted it has coordinated with nearby businesses and schools to ensure the intersection closure isn’t disruptive. “In addition to the road closure requirements, additional flagmen will be placed at the entrance of the Autospa,” project officials said in their online update to the community. “Additionally, construction notices were hand delivered to the impacted businesses, including Autospa, the school, gas station and Tim Hortons. 7-kilometre stretch of Ninth Line between Derry Road and Eglinton Avenue to four lanes from its current two-lane configuration. When completed in late 2027, the new-look north-south road will feature more than the two extra lanes — it’ll also include new sidewalks, cycle tracks for bike riders, better bus stops and a host of additional attributes expected to “promote growth and allow more housing in the area,” the City of Mississauga said earlier.

items.title: M City Development Adds Three More Towers After Urban Capital Buys Additional Mississauga Land
items.summary: Urban Capital says it has acquired more than four acres of land in Mississauga from its longtime development partner, Rogers Real Estate Development, to expand the M City project. According to the company, the new land will support three additional towers, named M6, M7 and M8, at the corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Confederation Parkway. Urban Capital did not disclose the financial terms of the deal. The company said two towers, M1 and M2, are already finished, M3 topped off last October, and M4 and M5 remain under construction. Urban Capital partner Mark Reeve said the firm has been involved with M City since the community broke ground in 2009 and credited Rogers for more than a decade of collaboration. Once complete, the company said M City is planned to include eight towers with more than 6,000 homes, retail and office space, and over two acres of public parkland.

items.title: Mississauga Bylaw Officials Remind Residents of New Fireworks Restrictions Ahead of Diwali
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is reminding residents to follow its fireworks bylaw as Diwali celebrations approach this week. According to the city, residents may only set off consumer fireworks on specific permitted holidays each year, and only on their own private property with the owner's permission. City officials said fireworks remain banned on all public property, including parks, streets, sidewalks and boulevards. This year, the city added Roman candles to its list of prohibited fireworks. Only adults 18 and older can buy fireworks, and only during the ten days leading up to an approved holiday, not on the holiday itself, the city said. The city is encouraging residents to consider quieter alternatives such as glow sticks and LED lights, which officials said are gentler on pets, wildlife and neighbours. Anyone who does set off permitted fireworks is asked to keep water on hand, supervise children closely and clean up thoroughly once the celebration ends. The reminder comes as part of the city's annual push to balance Diwali festivities with noise and fire safety concerns.

items.title: City of Mississauga Closes Ninth Line Intersection Near Ridgeway Plaza for Storm Sewer Work
items.summary: The City of Mississauga closed the intersection of Ninth Line and Platinum Drive, next to Ridgeway Plaza, from Nov. 2 to Nov. 7 to allow construction crews to keep working on the road's widening project. According to the city, the closure is needed to safely build a storm sewer system and an oil-grit separator structure at the intersection. City officials said drivers can detour via Eglinton Avenue and Ridgeway Drive while signs direct traffic around the closure. The city added that extra flaggers are posted at the entrance to the nearby Autospa, and that construction notices were hand-delivered to affected businesses, including Autospa, a nearby school, a gas station and a Tim Hortons. The broader project will widen a 7-kilometre stretch of Ninth Line between Derry Road and Eglinton Avenue from two lanes to four. Once finished in late 2027, the city said the rebuilt road will also include new sidewalks, cycle tracks and improved bus stops. Officials have said the upgrades are meant to support more housing and growth in the surrounding area.

items.title: Ontario Provincial Police Are Investigating a Fatal Early-Morning Crash in Puslinch That Killed Four Teenagers From the Mississauga Area
items.summary: Ontario Provincial Police say four teenagers are dead after a single-vehicle crash early Saturday morning on Watson Road South in Puslinch, near Guelph. According to OPP, the vehicle struck a guardrail before plunging into a ravine, killing a 19-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga, a 19-year-old man from Brampton, and a 15-year-old girl from Milton. Two other teenage girls, aged 15 and 16, survived the crash but were taken to hospital with serious, life-threatening injuries, police said. Investigators have not released a cause for the crash and have not said whether charges are expected. OPP confirmed the stretch of Watson Road South remained closed for several hours while officers investigated the scene. The force said updates would be provided as the investigation continues. The crash drew attention across the Peel and Halton regions given how many of the victims and survivors were local teenagers. Mississauga Insider will update this story if OPP releases further details.
